title: SEU Hardening Candidate Identification for a Controller/Datapath RTL Module
objective: Analyze the provided RTL module together with the accompanying fault model document, and produce a structured report that inventories every flip-flop group in the design, classifies each as control/state logic or data-pipeline logic, and recommends whether it should receive triple-modular-redundancy (TMR) hardening against single-event upsets (SEUs).
constraints: Do not edit any file under inputs/; submit only submission/vulnerability_report.json.
The RTL module must be treated as self-contained and synthesizable/simulatable with iverilog without external IP.
Register bit-widths and names referenced in the report must match those declared in controller_datapath.v exactly.

expected_outputs.description: A single JSON file at submission/vulnerability_report.json containing a flip-flop inventory, per-register classification (control_state or data_pipeline), TMR recommendation, and justification for each register group found in controller_datapath.v.

metrics.name: leakage_detection_accuracy
metrics.description: Fraction of the ground-truth control_state registers correctly identified and flagged tmr_recommended=true in the submission, relative to fabricated or missing entries.

metrics.name: fault_coverage
metrics.description: Proportion of all registers declared in controller_datapath.v that appear with a valid, schema-conformant entry in the submitted report (no omissions).

metrics.name: hardening_precision
metrics.description: Precision of TMR recommendations: correctly recommended control_state registers divided by total registers recommended for TMR, penalizing over-hardening of data-pipeline registers.

notes: evaluate.py reads the input artifacts under inputs/ for reference and grades submission/vulnerability_report.json for schema conformance and substantive correctness against a private ground-truth classification. A naive or empty submission is expected to fail grading.
